summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 58 (`ipns-signature-verify-coverage`) of CipherBox using the GSD workflow system — research, generate 4 PLAN.md files across 2 waves, verify them, then auto-chain into execution.
summary.outcome: Phase 58 was fully planned (4 plans, 2 waves, 0 blockers), all artifacts committed, and Wave 1 execution began with plan 58-01 spawned as a subagent; the transcript ends mid-execution before 58-01 returns.

repo: Phase 58 is a pure backend crypto/security coverage phase: TDD mode on, fine granularity, no UI, no schema-push, feature branch `feat/ipns-signature-verify-coverage`.
The local stack (redis:6380, api:3000, postgres, ipfs/kubo) was confirmed up, enabling 58-02's full-SDK-E2E gate to actually run.

Rust vector consumer (cross-language verify vectors) must live in `crates/fuse/tests/` not `crates/crypto/tests/` because `crates/crypto` cannot dev-depend on `api-client`/`core` — a real dependency-cycle constraint the planner caught and worked around.
9 FUSE unverified resolve sites exist; after the chokepoint is added, 8 are routed through `resolve_ipns_verified` (one is the folder-key descent hard-fail, handled separately).
RESEARCH.md `## Open Questions` section must carry a `(RESOLVED)` marker after planning or the plan-checker flags a cosmetic warning — a doc hygiene requirement in the GSD verification gate.
The `commit_failed` return from the commit helper is a known false-negative; always verify with `git log` rather than retrying the commit.

code.finding: New CBOR cid/sequence decoder lives here (plan 58-01); provides the binding that `resolve_ipns_verified` in `crates/fuse` depends on.
`resolve_ipns_verified` chokepoint wrapper added here; 8 existing unverified resolve call-sites in FUSE are routed through it as part of 58-01.
Cross-language verify vector tests (7 cases, Rust + sdk-core, plan 58-04) placed here rather than `crates/crypto/tests` to avoid the crypto→api-client dev-dependency cycle.
`## Open Questions` heading needed `(RESOLVED)` appended inline; without it the plan-checker emits a warning that blocks clean verification.
Frontmatter filled by orchestrator (Nyquist enabled); body scaffold is owned by execute/validate tooling, not the planner.

workflow: For security/crypto phases, sequential executors on the feature branch are preferred over parallel worktree agents to avoid cwd-drift, merge failures, and stranded worktrees — correctness over speed.
The `commit_failed` response from GSD's commit helper is a known false-negative pattern; the canonical fix is to verify with `git log` and not retry.
Fixing a cosmetic plan-checker warning (doc heading marker) directly in the file is cheaper than burning a full planner revision cycle — the checker green-lights execution if no blockers exist.
AUTO_MODE (`--auto`) skips human checkpoints at most gates, but 58-02 still emits a hard checkpoint at the D-10 full-SDK-E2E gate regardless of AUTO_MODE.
Pattern mapper output (PATTERNS.md, 14 files classified) feeds directly into the planner prompt — running it before spawning the planner is a required pre-planning step when no PATTERNS.md exists.

friction: `commit_failed` false-negative from the commit helper required a manual `git log` verification step and introduced uncertainty about whether the commit actually landed.
RESEARCH.md `## Open Questions` heading missing the `(RESOLVED)` marker caused a plan-checker warning that required a separate edit + commit cycle after verification, adding latency.

The dependency-cycle constraint (crypto can't dev-depend on api-client/core) was discovered during planning rather than captured in CONTEXT.md, requiring the planner to adapt the test file location mid-plan.
open_items: Plan 58-02 will pause at the D-10 human checkpoint (full-SDK-E2E gate); requires local stack to be up (docker compose + API + redis 6380) when that plan runs.
Wave 1 plan 58-01 was spawned but had not returned at transcript end — execution outcome unknown.
Wave 2 plans 58-03 (web/sdk-core resolve dedup) and 58-04 (cross-language verify vectors, 7 cases) not yet executed.
The Rust vector consumer location workaround (`crates/fuse/tests/` instead of `crates/crypto/tests/`) should be revisited if the crate dependency graph changes to allow a cleaner placement.
